note: Six ways a replay can end, decided server-side from what she actually did. Ordered by priority; the first match wins. Deliberately NOT ranked by money - 'steady_hand' is the catch-all and is written as the best outcome, because sitting still through a drop is the skill. Nia narrates all six; there is no score and no prize.

endings.title: A Lucky Run
endings.speaker: coach
lines: You finished up more than ten percent. That's a real result and you should enjoy it.
I do want to name how you got there, though: you put nearly everything on one company and held your breath.
endings.next: That worked this time. It is not a method, and it does not come twice in a row. Try the same run at half the size and see how different it feels.
endings.coach_coda: Getting a good result from a risky process is the most dangerous way to learn, because it teaches you the wrong lesson.

endings.title: Patience Paid
endings.speaker: coach
lines: You finished up more than ten percent, and you did it without panicking or piling in.
You sized the position so a bad week could not hurt you, and then you left it alone.
endings.next: That is the whole method. It is unglamorous and it repeats, which is exactly why it works.
endings.coach_coda: You did that with a plan, not a hunch. That's the part that repeats.

endings.title: Sold At The Bottom
endings.speaker: coach
lines: You sold at the lowest point of the whole replay.
Look at what the days after that looked like. I'm not showing you this to make you feel bad - I'm showing you because the shape of it is the lesson.
endings.loss: the difference between where you sold and where it ended
endings.next: The dip was temporary. The decision you made inside it was not. Next time, decide what you'll do before the number goes red.
endings.coach_coda: Everyone does this once. The people who keep investing are the ones who did it once and understood why. You just did.

endings.title: Never Started
endings.speaker: coach
lines: You finished with exactly what you started with. Not a cent lost.
Also not a thing learned, and that is the part that actually costs money over a lifetime.
endings.next: Nothing here can hurt you. Go back and buy one share of anything - the smallest amount you like - just to see what happens.
endings.coach_coda: Sitting out feels free. It is the one choice in here with a cost you never see.

endings.title: A Real Loss
endings.speaker: coach
lines: You finished down more than ten percent. That is a genuine loss and I am not going to dress it up.
You also held your nerve while it fell, which is more than most people manage. It simply kept falling.
endings.loss: more than a tenth of what you started with
endings.next: This happens, it will happen again, and it is not a verdict on you. What changes the outcome next time is the size you choose at the start, not how well you predict.
endings.coach_coda: The money here was never real. What you now know about how you react when it drops is.

endings.title: A Steady Hand
endings.speaker: coach
lines: You finished somewhere in the middle. No dramatic win, no damage.
Which sounds like nothing happened - but you watched a number go red and you did not flinch, and you did not chase it either.
endings.next: That is the hardest thing in here, and it is the thing that compounds. Most of investing looks exactly like this.
endings.coach_coda: Sitting still while a number goes red is the whole skill. You have it.
